manual.gtcsolo.chapter.traits.body:
§lAbout Traits§r

Mobs in this world carry levels and §dtraits§r. The higher the level, the more — and the nastier — the traits.

Traits trample vanilla common sense without hesitation. Some turn magic into healing, some swap places with you, some crush your soul along with your revival items... check the traits before fighting anything unfamiliar.

§e◆ How to check§r
Look at a mob to see its trait icons.

§e◆ Danger level§r
The more advanced skills you take from the upgrade tree, the more dangerous nearby spawns become. Power comes with risk.

§e◆ This encyclopedia§r
Pick a trait from the list on the left. §6Min Lv§r is the mob level at which the trait can start appearing.

manual.gtcsolo.chapter.world.body:
§lAbout this World§r

This is not the usual AllTheGregTech. §6gtcsolo§r rewrites it from the ground up.

§e◆ Upgrade Tree§r
Open with §bK§r. Earning XP grants skill/stat points to buy permanent upgrades. Advancements also give XP.

§e◆ Fantasy Equipment§r
Fantasy weapons and armor have been wiped and rebuilt with this world's own balance. Weapons grow as you use them.

§e◆ Smaller changes§r
- Beds cannot be used until deep night (14500t)
- Custom stats such as Lucky Hit exist
- Mobs carry traits (see "About Traits")

(More to come)
manual.gtcsolo.chapter.wen.body:
§lAbout WEN§r

§dWEN§r (Wireless Energy Network) is a custom system that sends and receives EU wirelessly.

§e◆ Core§r
The §bWEN Main Storage§r (multiblock) is the heart of a network. Set the network ID from the WEN Data Monitor. Energy cells expand capacity.

§e◆ Transfer§r
- §bWEN Wireless Input§r — receives EU and forwards it to storage
- §bWEN Wireless Output§r — draws EU from storage into cables
- Energy/dynamo hatches for multiblocks exist at each voltage

§e◆ Bridging other energy§r
- FE wireless ports — connect FE machines directly
- AE ports / §bWEN Wireless Energy Card§r — powers an entire AE2 grid (2 AE = 1 EU)

§e◆ Mass production§r
WEN equipment is integrated and mass-produced in the WEN Nexus Assembler.

gtcsolo.machine.hpabf.desc.1: §bMultiblock Performance:§r Coil-based heat control; the coil's EU consumption discount applies.
gtcsolo.machine.hpabf.desc.2: §e[Power Resistance]§r Due to the massive coils' resistance, OC cannot be performed normally — only imperfect OCs occur (§c×0.65§r per step).
gtcsolo.machine.hpabf.desc.3: §e[Heat Rise]§r To run a recipe, the machine first generates the recipe's required heat via power. Each OC step raises the temperature by §b(T+100K) × 1.3§r (cumulative — +100K added before each multiplication).
gtcsolo.machine.hpabf.desc.4: §e[Promotion]§r For every §b1000K§r the temperature exceeds the recipe's requirement, one imperfect OC is converted into one §aperfect OC§r (×0.25).
gtcsolo.machine.hpabf.desc.5: §e[Temperature Bonus]§r When the actual heat is §btwice or more§r the recipe's required heat, separately from OC the recipe duration is reduced to §a80%%§r of original.
gtcsolo.machine.hpabf.desc.6: §e[Coil Cap]§r Since heat is coil-controlled, it is subject to the coil's temperature limit.
gtcsolo.machine.hpabf.desc.7: §6Structural boost:§r Proper heat treatment and robust construction raise the coil's effective heat limit to §b150%%§r of normal.

gtcsolo.ical.description.1: An advanced circuit production line derived from the assembly line. Supports circuit assembler and circuit assembly line recipes.
gtcsolo.ical.description.4: Allows overclocking and parallel operation without an additional machine-specific tier or parallel cap.
gtcsolo.ical.description.5: Uses the structure's mass production mechanism for bulk production.
gtcsolo.ical.description.6: Base IO bonus: 8. Each module and overclock adds 8. Multiply IO by the parallel count; only the parallel count multiplies overclocked EU/t.
gtcsolo.ical.description.9: Overclocking and parallel operation are disabled.
gtcsolo.ical.description.10: Uses the whole machine to manufacture advanced circuits.
gtcsolo.ical.description.11: Requires ordered baseline inputs and research data. Each module grants two additional recipe copies, up to 13 copies including the baseline.
gtcsolo.ical.description.12: Supply the upper input buses before processing finishes to claim additional copies.
gtcsolo.ical.description.13: Each contribution consumes exactly one full recipe worth of items and fluids.
gtcsolo.ical.description.14: A single upper fluid hatch can supply multiple contributions.
gtcsolo.ical.description.15: Only contributions actually received are included in the finished output.
gtcsolo.ical.description.18: Circuit research data must match the output item.
gtcsolo.ical.description.19: Insert ordinary assembly-line research media into an item input bus to start EU-powered analysis. Permanent circuit data stays in data hatches; temporary circuit data stays in the core. Analysis can only unlock manufacturing recipes rated at UHV or below. UEV and higher recipes require circuit research data in a data hatch.
gtcsolo.ical.description.22: The line also learns from continued circuit manufacture.
gtcsolo.ical.description.23: Repeated production accumulates recipe records and reduces processing time.
gtcsolo.ical.description.24: Passing 5, 15 and 30 completions grants increasingly strong duration reductions.
gtcsolo.ical.description.25: The core holds two recipe records and two temporary research media. While idle, each record loses one completion per recorded processing duration. Completing one recipe also reduces the other record. When a Circuit Data Orb supplies the research, each completed batch is also recorded on that orb. Its saved counts do not decay during idle time or production of other recipes and can be used again. Copying research data does not copy these manufacturing counts.
gtcsolo.ical.description.26: Temporary media are returned through an output bus when their production record expires. Incoming third data occupies a zero-completion record and displaces the oldest.
gtcsolo.ical.tooltip.summary: Circuit assembly, advanced circuit production and research data analysis.
gtcsolo.ical.tooltip.detail: Full description: JEI uses (U) → Multiblock Introduction
gtcsolo.ismbf.name: Industrial Superheated Massive Blast Furnace
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.1: The pinnacle of blast furnaces. Supports sub-tick processing, parallel operation, and laser energy hatches.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.2: Handles all furnace recipe types. Temperature and other operating conditions are independent of the selected recipe mode.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.5: This immense furnace requires internal heat before it can operate.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.6: The furnace starts without heat. Power received through energy hatches is converted at 500 EU per 1 F. When no recipe is running and no power is supplied, temperature decreases by 7% per second. The temperature limit equals the coil temperature.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.9: Runs alongside other recipe types, except while an extreme-temperature blast furnace recipe is running.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.10: Starts with an input/output bonus of up to 4096, adjusted to available materials and output space. Parallel operation also affects it.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.11: Sub-tick parallel operation does not apply.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.12: Above 10000 F, smelting duration is fixed at 1 tick. While no other recipe type is running, temperatures above 10000/12000/14000 F grant a separate parallel factor of 4/16/64, multiplied by external parallel operation.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.15: Uses the furnace temperature. Starts with an input/output bonus of up to 64, affected by parallel operation.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.16: Energy discounts are converted into shorter processing time. Total EU consumption remains the same as it would with those energy discounts.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.17: Sub-tick parallel operation is available for these recipes.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.18: Grants one perfect overclock for every 1800 F above the recipe's required temperature.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.19: Above 10000 F, processing time is reduced to 75% of its original duration.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.22: Uses the furnace temperature. Starts with an input/output bonus of up to 64, affected by parallel operation.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.23: Energy discounts are converted into stronger processing-time reductions, consuming less total EU than the original energy discounts would.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.24: Grants one perfect overclock for every 1800 F above the recipe's required temperature.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.25: Above 10000/12000/14000 F, processing time is reduced to 80/75/66% of its original duration.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.28: For metals that melt only at extreme temperatures.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.29: Requires the furnace's maximum permitted temperature throughout operation.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.30: Overclocking beyond the energy hatch limit and all parallel operation, including sub-tick parallel operation, are disabled.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.31: Operates beyond the furnace's temperature limit, requiring cooling during processing.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.32: Accepts distilled water, PCB coolant, and europium as coolants, each with a different cooling efficiency.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.33: Insufficient cooling increases damage according to operating temperature. At 100% damage, the furnace overheats, powers down, fails the recipe, and begins cooling. Once temperature reaches ambient or lower, overheating clears and damage slowly recovers.
gtcsolo.ismbf.description.34: §4Restarting the furnace before overheating has cleared causes a massive explosion.§r
gtcsolo.ismbf.tooltip.summary: A massive blast furnace supporting sub-tick processing, parallel operation, and laser energy hatches

gtcsolo.iterative_assembly.description.1: Processes Assembly Line recipes without ordered material inputs. Ordinary Assembly Line research data is still required.
gtcsolo.iterative_assembly.description.2: Each normal overclock multiplies EU/t by 4 and processing speed by 1.8.
gtcsolo.iterative_assembly.description.3: Place output samples in the input bus above the core. An output qualifies for 2.25x OC speed per stage when its sample count is at least the number of distinct item types in that bus. EU/t still increases by 4. With 64 types, each output you want to improve needs 64 samples.
gtcsolo.iterative_assembly.description.4: Samples are not consumed and their bus does not supply recipe materials. Stacks of the same item are counted as one type and their quantities are added together. NBT differences are ignored.
gtcsolo.iterative_assembly.description.5: The sample is checked when processing starts. Changing it during a job affects the next job.
gtcsolo.iterative_assembly.description.6: Requires at least 115 Large-Scale Assembler Casings. Only casing positions accept interchangeable IO, energy, and data hatches.
gtcsolo.iterative_assembly.description.7: Both the material input bus below the core and the sample input bus above it accept any tier. Only the bus directly above this core is checked for samples. Requires one data access hatch.
gtcsolo.iterative_assembly.description.8: Does not perform sub-tick processing or parallel-hatch parallelization.

gtcsolo.room.farming.description.1: All voltage casings and glass must share a tier. Tempered glass counts as LV; laminated glass as HV.
gtcsolo.room.farming.description.2: Supports industrial overclocking. Operating voltage is capped by both power supply and structure grade.
gtcsolo.room.farming.description.3: Supports parallel hatches and sub-tick processing. Fertilizer and culture supplies scale with the processed quantity. Seeds are not consumed.
gtcsolo.room.farming.description.4: Handles mineral crops. IV and higher mineral seeds require a Farming Room; food and other crops retain their existing cultivation paths.
gtcsolo.room.construction.description.1: Requires matching casing and glass grades. Structure grade caps voltage. Supports industrial OC and parallel processing.
gtcsolo.room.construction.description.2: Use coils that meet the recipe's temperature requirement. Insufficient heat prevents processing.
gtcsolo.room.construction.description.3: Every 900K above the recipe requirement improves one industrial overclock's duration factor to 0.85.
gtcsolo.room.construction.description.4: Base input/output bonus is 4, increasing by 2 for every 900K above the recipe requirement. It multiplies with industrial OC, hatch parallels and sub-tick batches.
gtcsolo.room.construction.description.5: Mineral, metal and gem essence conversions are exclusive to this room. Food and other conversions remain unchanged.
gtcsolo.lcr.introduction.1: Has perfect overclocking and a compact structure that is easy to build and allows flexible placement of functional hatches. Some recipes can only be run in the Large Chemical Reactor, making it particularly important for progression.
gtcsolo.font_compare.title: Font Comparison (Temporary)
gtcsolo.ebf.introduction.1: Produces aluminium and higher-tier metals and alloys. It can be used during LV: two LV Energy Input Hatches raise its operating voltage so that it can run MV recipes. Better coils allow hotter recipes, improve overclocking efficiency and reduce power consumption. Higher-performance coils also cost more, making shared walls between furnaces an important way to save materials.
gtcsolo.pyrolyse_oven.introduction.1: Uses heat to process logs and other materials. Adding nitrogen allows faster recipes, while better coils increase processing speed.
gtcsolo.cracker.introduction.1: Improves yields from oil processing, producing more cracked fluid per unit of feedstock than the equivalent Chemical Reactor process. The choice of hydrogen or steam, and how heavily the feedstock is cracked, changes the proportions obtained through distillation. Choose the cracking and distillation route to suit the products you need. Better coils reduce power consumption.
gtcsolo.cleanroom.introduction.1: Provides the clean environment required for processing inside. A correctly built and powered room purifies its interior; recipes requiring a cleanroom can run once cleanliness reaches 90%. The machines inside need their own power supply, separate from the purification equipment. Machine Hulls and Diodes can carry power through the walls. Opening and closing installed doors does not reduce cleanliness.
gtcsolo.cleanroom.introduction.3: • An invalid structure loses its accumulated cleanliness. Take care when breaking structure blocks.
gtcsolo.cleanroom.introduction.4: • The interior must remain clean. Contaminating machines, such as generators and machines with mufflers, prevent the cleanroom from operating.
gtcsolo.cleanroom.introduction.5: • The room can be resized to provide the space you need, but larger rooms take longer to purify.
gtcsolo.assembly_line.introduction.1: Assembles higher-tier components and machines. Running a recipe requires the corresponding research data as well as its materials.
gtcsolo.assembly_line.introduction.2: Create research data with a Scanner or Research Station and place it in a Data Access Hatch. Research Station research also requires a supply of computation.
gtcsolo.assembly_line.introduction.3: Supply items to ULV Input Buses in recipe order, from the controller end toward the output end. Automation must route each ingredient to its assigned bus.
gtcsolo.assembly_line.introduction.4: Fluids do not require an input order and can be supplied together through multi-fluid input hatches.
gtcsolo.assembly_line.introduction.5: Extend the middle section to add ingredient positions, choosing the line length to suit what you intend to produce. Click the P button in the JEI structure display to inspect different lengths.
An essential progression machine at the heart of oil processing. It requires a large amount of stainless steel, but sharing exterior walls can reduce that cost in exchange for some restrictions on functional hatch placement. Multi-fluid output hatches cannot be used, so the machine requires enough fluid output hatches for the recipe. These features give it a variable-length section, which can be inspected by clicking the P button in the JEI multiblock structure display.
gtcsolo.large_boiler.introduction.1: Burns solid fuels or supported fluid fuels to produce large amounts of steam from water. Steam production rises as the boiler heats up, making it suited to continuous operation. The throttle adjusts steam production and fuel consumption.
gtcsolo.large_boiler.introduction.3: • Maintain an uninterrupted water supply. The boiler continues to consume water while cooling after shutdown. Restoring water after a hot boiler has run dry causes an explosion. If it runs dry, stop combustion and let it cool fully before refilling.
gtcsolo.large_turbine.introduction.1: Generates power by using the appropriate fuel to spin a Turbine Rotor. The rotor and Rotor Holder determine output and fuel efficiency; output rises as the rotor gains speed after startup. Provide enough fuel flow and Dynamo Hatch output capacity for the chosen setup, and replace the rotor as it wears out.
gtcsolo.large_turbine.introduction.3: • Install a Turbine Rotor in the Rotor Holder and keep the 3×3 area directly in front of it clear. Right-clicking a spinning Rotor Holder causes damage. Wait for rotation to stop before replacing the rotor.
gtcsolo.fusion.introduction.1: Uses fusion reactions to produce advanced materials and plasma. Starting a recipe requires a large amount of EU in addition to the power consumed during operation.
gtcsolo.fusion.introduction.limits: Supports recipes up to %s. With %s Energy Input Hatches, the reactor stores up to %sM EU.
gtcsolo.fusion.introduction.expand_stora: Adding Energy Input Hatches increases stored EU capacity, allowing recipes with larger startup energy requirements.
gtcsolo.fusion.introduction.fixed_hatche: All %s Energy Input Hatches are required. Overclocking is not available.
gtcsolo.fusion.introduction.2: Continuous operation preserves heat, but stopping and cooling requires startup EU again. The reactor mark determines its voltage limit; higher-tier Energy Input Hatches alone cannot raise that limit.
gtcsolo.research_station.introduction.1: Produces advanced research data for the Assembly Line. Place the research sample and the appropriate Data Orb or Data Module in the Object Holder, then supply both power and computation.
gtcsolo.research_station.introduction.2: The supplied computation must meet the recipe's minimum CWU/t. Supplying more computation speeds up research. Use the completed research data in an Assembly Line to run the corresponding recipe.
gtcsolo.research_station.introduction.3: Precautions: Face the Object Holder in the opposite direction from the controller. The research sample is consumed when research finishes.
gtcsolo.network_switch.introduction.1: Combines computation from multiple High Performance Computation Arrays (HPCAs), allowing research that exceeds one array's capacity or distribution to several consumers. Connect Computation Data Reception Hatches toward the providers and Computation Data Transmission Hatches toward the consumers.
gtcsolo.network_switch.introduction.2: Each connected HPCA needs an HPCA Bridge Component, and the Network Switch needs its own power supply. Consumers share the available computation; adding branches does not increase the total supply.
gtcsolo.hpca.introduction.1: Supplies computation to Research Stations and other consumers. Fill its nine component positions with computation, cooling and bridge components, choosing a combination that balances the required computation with enough cooling.
gtcsolo.hpca.introduction.2: Power consumption and heat generation vary with computation load, and upkeep power is consumed even while idle. Size the power supply and cooling for the intended workload. Hover over the component grid in the center of the interface to inspect maximum computation, cooling demand, cooling capacity and coolant requirements.
gtcsolo.hpca.introduction.4: • Maintain the PCB Coolant supply when using active cooling. Insufficient cooling can overheat and damage components, reducing available computation.
gtcsolo.computation.introduction.1: CWU/t is the computation supplied each tick; total CWU is the work needed to finish research. The minimum CWU/t must be met to operate, and a larger supply completes the required total CWU sooner. Computation is supplied when needed and cannot be stored for later use.
gtcsolo.computation.introduction.2: Connect an HPCA's Computation Data Transmission Hatch to the consumer's Computation Data Reception Hatch with Optical Fiber Cable. The High Performance Computation Array (HPCA) and the consumer each need a separate power supply as well as the computation connection.
gtcsolo.computation.introduction.3: A Network Switch can combine computation from multiple HPCAs and distribute it to several consumers. Machines operating at the same time share the available supply. Plan capacity around each consumer's minimum CWU/t and the research speed you need.
gtcsolo.hpca_components.introduction.1: HPCA Computation Components provide computation. HPCA Advanced Computation Components provide more computation per position, but also require more power and cooling.
gtcsolo.hpca_components.introduction.2: HPCA Heat Sink Components provide cooling without coolant. HPCA Active Cooling Components consume PCB Coolant to provide greater cooling capacity.
gtcsolo.hpca_components.introduction.3: An HPCA Bridge Component is required to combine and distribute computation through a Network Switch. It is not required for a direct connection to a Research Station.
gtcsolo.hpca_components.introduction.4: Fill unused positions with Empty HPCA Components. Components work the same in any of the nine positions; their types and quantities determine performance.

gtcsolo.wen.introduction.1: A shared energy reserve connecting generators and distant machines. Collect power from multiple sites and supply equipment through wireless inputs, outputs, and dedicated hatches.
gtcsolo.wen.introduction.2: Structure: Build a closed cuboid with each outer dimension between 3 and 15 blocks, fill its interior with energy cells, and install exactly one WEN Data Monitor. The controller can replace any shell block, including the roof, floor, edges, and corners.
gtcsolo.wen.introduction.3: Storage: The WEN Basic Energy Cell, Lapotronic Capacitors, and Ultimate Capacitors can be mixed in the interior. Capacity depends on their types and quantities. The linked energy cell page lists the supported blocks.
gtcsolo.wen.introduction.4: Power transfer: After forming the structure, set a network ID at the monitor and select that ID on connected devices. Collect power through wireless inputs, then deliver it through wireless outputs or energy hatches. Observe each device's voltage and amperage ratings. After renaming a network, select its new ID on connected devices.
gtcsolo.wen.introduction.5: Expansion: Use Fantasy Cores at the monitor to increase capacity. An Evernight Crystal enables connections across dimensions. Use the corresponding ports or a WEN Wireless Energy Card to connect FE or AE equipment.
gtcsolo.wen.introduction.6: Caution: Breaking the structure stops supply from the network while retaining stored energy. Reforming with a smaller capacity, including replacing cells with lower-capacity ones, discards energy above the new limit. Check the remaining charge before downsizing.
gtcsolo.glossary.wen_cells.title: WEN Energy Cells
gtcsolo.glossary.wen_cells.overview: Storage blocks placed inside WEN Main Storage. These seven types can be mixed. Each capacity is per block, before monitor upgrades.
gtcsolo.glossary.wen_cells.note: Empty capacitors are not accepted. Fill every interior position with an energy cell. Increase capacity by expanding the interior, using higher-capacity cells, or applying upgrades at the monitor.
